Occasionally in Phl Mss scribes confuse t and p , especially when the former is part of a ligature. I have no solid suggestion for YfnTEº, unless, partially with Nyberg, it stands for ºgatas 'having gone.' He might have announced himself at court with pātrâgato'smi 'I have come as minister' and this was taken as his title. This would make sense of the inexplicable zīwā wuzurgmihr YfnTER__TXt ī amāh (§8). That is, Xursraw, knowing that the Persians have won, ironically refers to his vizier with the Indian title.
